groups.name: East Lisbon and Parque das Nações

neighborhoods.name: Baixa and Chiado
neighborhoods.tip: Flat, central and walkable, between the river and the hills. Most sights are a short walk or tram ride.

neighborhoods.name: Alfama and Graça
neighborhoods.tip: Steep lanes and fado houses below the castle. Cars cannot reach many streets, so give drivers the nearest square.

neighborhoods.name: Bairro Alto and Príncipe Real
neighborhoods.tip: Boutiques, gardens and viewpoints by day. Bairro Alto gets loud late at night, Príncipe Real stays calmer.

neighborhoods.name: Avenida da Liberdade
neighborhoods.tip: A leafy boulevard of designer shops, with Metro stations along it.

neighborhoods.name: Cais do Sodré
neighborhoods.tip: By the river, next to the Time Out Market and the station for trains to Belém and Cascais.

neighborhoods.name: Estrela and Lapa
neighborhoods.tip: Calm and residential, with a big park and the domed Estrela Basilica. Tram 28 passes by.

neighborhoods.name: Belém
neighborhoods.tip: Monuments by the river, west of the center. Quiet in the evening; the center is a tram, train or taxi ride away.

neighborhoods.name: Parque das Nações
neighborhoods.tip: Modern riverside district by the Oceanário, close to the airport and Oriente station, where trains leave for the Algarve.

neighborhoods.name: Cascais (by the sea)
neighborhoods.tip: A seaside town west of Lisbon, connected by train from Cais do Sodré.

neighborhoods.name: Sintra
neighborhoods.tip: Palaces in the hills. Trains run to Lisbon from Sintra station.

airports.name: Lisbon airport (Humberto Delgado)
airports.tip: Taxis and ride-hailing pickups are outside arrivals. The Metro red line also runs from the airport into the city.

stations.name: Oriente station
stations.tip: Main station for trains to the Algarve.

items.title: Taxis
items.text: Licensed taxis are metered. In Lisbon you can hail one with its roof light on, find one at a rank, or call. Ride-hailing apps such as Uber and Bolt also operate.

items.title: Metro and trams
items.text: The Metro covers the center and the airport. Buy a reusable card at any Metro station and top it up. Tram 28 is scenic and very crowded, so watch your bag.

items.title: Hills
items.text: Lisbon is steep, and the limestone pavements get slippery. Flat shoes with grip help. The Glória and Bica funiculars and the Santa Justa lift save some climbs.

items.title: Trains out of town
items.text: Sintra trains leave from Rossio. Cascais and Belém trains leave from Cais do Sodré. Algarve trains leave from Oriente.

taxi_tariff.note: Rough estimate from Portugal's new national taxi tariff and straight-line distance. The new tariff is rolling out during 2026, so some meters may still use the old one. The meter decides.
taxi_tariff.source: AMT Regulamento n.º 717/2026, as reported by e-konomista.pt and tradersunion.com

items.title: Private driver or taxi
items.text: About 3 hours by road to Faro and a little more to Lagos (estimate). Agree the price before you set off; many travelers pre-book a transfer.

items.title: Train
items.text: CP trains run from Lisbon Oriente to Faro: about 3 hours on the Alfa Pendular, about 3.5 hours on the Intercidades. Fares usually from about €29. For Lagos, change at Tunes.
items.source: everyrail.com Lisbon to Faro guide; CP

items.title: Express coach
items.text: Express coaches link Lisbon with the main Algarve towns.

items.title: Rental car
items.text: The Algarve's A22 motorway has electronic tolls only. Ask the rental company about a toll device.

hero.caption: Ponta da Piedade
hero.alt: Pen and ink sketch of sea stacks and cliffs at Ponta da Piedade

neighborhoods.name: Lagos
neighborhoods.tip: Old town walls, the Ponta da Piedade cliffs and plenty of restaurants. A good base for the west.

neighborhoods.name: Sagres
neighborhoods.tip: Wild cliffs, surf beaches and sunsets near Cape St Vincent. Quieter, with fewer services.

neighborhoods.name: Portimão and Praia da Rocha
neighborhoods.tip: A working town with a long beach, and many boat trips to the caves.

neighborhoods.name: Carvoeiro and Lagoa
neighborhoods.tip: Closest base to the Benagil caves and the Seven Hanging Valleys trail.

neighborhoods.name: Albufeira
neighborhoods.tip: The busiest resort, with an old town and big beaches. Central for day trips both ways.

neighborhoods.name: Vilamoura and Quarteira
neighborhoods.tip: Marina, golf and resort hotels, near Praia da Falésia.

neighborhoods.name: Faro
neighborhoods.tip: The airport city, with a walled old town and boats into the Ria Formosa lagoon.

neighborhoods.name: Tavira
neighborhoods.tip: A calm, elegant river town. Island beaches are a short ferry ride away.

neighborhoods.name: Not sure yet, or somewhere else

airports.name: Faro airport
airports.tip: Taxis wait outside arrivals. Faro town is a short ride; Lagos and Tavira are much longer drives, so many travelers pre-book a transfer.

items.title: Taxis and private drivers
items.text: Towns are spread out along the coast, so rides between them add up. For longer trips, agree the price first or book a transfer. Ride-hailing apps work in the bigger towns; in small villages, ask your hotel to call a taxi.

items.title: Regional train
items.text: A regional CP line runs along the coast between Lagos, Faro and Tavira. It is slow but easy, and stations are not always close to the beaches.

items.title: Driving
items.text: A rental car gives the most freedom for cliffs and beaches. The A22 motorway uses electronic tolls only, so ask the rental company about a toll device.

items.title: Boats
items.text: Cave, coast and lagoon trips leave from Lagos, Portimão, Benagil, Faro, Olhão and Tavira.

taxi_tariff.note: Rough estimate from Portugal's new national taxi tariff and straight-line distance. Towns may set local variations, and some meters may still use the old tariff during 2026. Long rides between towns are often quoted as a fixed price; agree it first.
taxi_tariff.source: AMT Regulamento n.º 717/2026, as reported by e-konomista.pt and tradersunion.com
